gaps.need: Primary source-backed decision rule distinguishing Fisher exact from chi-square for sparse contingency tables.
gaps.reason: Current corpus source extracted for chi-square provides expected-count conditions but does not provide a sufficiently explicit Fisher-exact decision rule in the extracted text.

resolution.note: NIST provides the primary exact-test rule for small independent 2x2 discrete data; Penn State provides supporting guidance that Fisher's exact method is an alternative when the large-sample two-proportion approximation condition is not met. No universal total-sample cutoff is encoded.

resolution.note: Schober et al. directly support Spearman for ordinal data, nonnormal continuous data, relevant outliers, and nonlinear monotonic relationships, with graphical/form and independence checks. No normality-p-value switch rule is encoded.

gaps.need: Primary source-backed decision rule for when negative-binomial regression should replace or supplement Poisson regression, including overdispersion diagnostics.
gaps.reason: A specialist source now directly supports quasi-Poisson and negative-binomial regression as alternatives for overdispersed counts and explains their different mean-variance relationships. A fully automated negative-binomial selection rule still needs operational diagnostics for matching variance structure and other count-data features.

resolution_progress.note: Ver Hoef & Boveng (2007) supports overdispersion-aware model selection but does not justify the crude rule 'overdispersion => negative binomial'.

gaps.need: Source-backed operational guidance for dispersion assessment, excess zeros, and model adequacy before automated Poisson recommendation.
gaps.reason: The specialist source supports detecting overdispersion as a reason to reconsider ordinary Poisson and comparing quasi-Poisson versus negative-binomial variance structures. Excess-zero handling and a complete automated adequacy workflow remain unresolved.

resolution_progress.note: Overdispersion now has direct source support; excess zeros and full operational thresholds remain open.

gaps.reason: Current logistic-regression sources support binary-outcome routing and general diagnostics but do not yet provide a sufficiently explicit Methodome rule for separation detection and response.

resolution.note: The corpus now supports detection/guarding of complete and quasi-complete separation and blocks ordinary maximum-likelihood interpretation under separation. Firth is recorded as a candidate remedy, not yet as an automatically executable Methodome fallback.

gaps.need: Primary source-backed safeguard for sparse-event and small-sample logistic regression, including when ordinary maximum-likelihood estimates may be biased or unstable and when penalized or small-sample alternatives should be considered.
gaps.reason: Current corpus material does not yet support an operational rare-event or sparse-event threshold or automatic fallback method.

resolution.note: The safeguard explicitly rejects a universal 10-EPV cutoff and instead treats sparse-event risk as multifactorial. Firth is source-supported as a candidate remedy but remains outside automatic execution until implemented and validated.
